title: PolySync idea validation vision
input: An expanded 'super-app' narrative for PolySync drafted in a DeepSeek conversation (shared 2026-09-24). It added martial-arts AI shadowing, a global coach marketplace, computer vision trained on social-media video, a McKay athlete-tier model, body-photo tracking, a 'Maldini golden ratio' for youth football and a five-region launch. It is treated here as a set of hypotheses to check, not as evidence.

verdict.headline: The core idea holds. The super-app expansion is not validated.
verdict.summary: The hybrid engine, the coach in the loop and the club buyer are backed by evidence, CI and a market scan. The expansion bundles five businesses into one launch across five regions for one engineer; three of its load-bearing claims are unverifiable or wrong, one statistic contradicts itself, and three ideas cross legal or safety lines. It also reopens ADR-005, which already narrowed PolySync to one sport context and one beachhead.

verdictScale.validated: Checked against a primary source; holds
verdictScale.real-constraint: True, and it changes what we build
verdictScale.plausible: Reasonable but untested; needs its own test
verdictScale.misread: The source is real but says something different
verdictScale.misused: A real framework applied where it does not fit
verdictScale.unverified: No source found; do not repeat it
verdictScale.folklore: Widely repeated; cannot have been measured
verdictScale.not-feasible: Current technology cannot deliver it reliably
verdictScale.thin-margin: Possible, but the economics barely work
verdictScale.red-line: Legal or safety line; do not build

claims.claim: Google searches for 'hybrid athlete' tripled between Dec 2025 and Apr 2026
claims.check: No source found for the figure
claims.implication: Drop it from any pitch. HYROX participation (MKT-001, MKT-005) is the verified demand signal.

repair.fix: Replace the unsourced search figure with demand signals that can be proved: HYROX participation, a dated Google Trends export run and archived by us, and pilot waitlist sign-ups
repair.restated: Hybrid racing participation is growing, including in the UAE
repair.proof: Waitlist sign-up rate in the UAE pilot clubs

claims.claim: The interference dogma is overturned: concurrent training doesn't impair strength or muscle
claims.check: The 2022 meta-analysis (43 studies) finds no loss of hypertrophy or maximal strength, but explosive strength is attenuated (SMD -0.28), more so when both are trained in the same session
claims.implication: This framing argues against PolySync. The accurate version, 'mostly compatible except power and timing', is why the engine exists (rules H1, H2).

repair.fix: State the science accurately: strength and endurance are mostly compatible, except explosive power and hard sessions close together. That is the engine's reason to exist
repair.restated: Concurrent training is mostly compatible, except power and session timing, which the engine manages
repair.proof: Already sourced; engine rules H1 and H2 enforce it in CI

claims.claim: No app has solved martial-arts coaching; 0% of martial-arts gyms coach online
claims.check: The 0% figure is not in the source it points to. Several AI martial-arts and boxing apps are already on the stores
claims.implication: The gap is not that nobody built it; it is that it does not work well yet.

repair.fix: Drop the 0% figure. The gap is trust, not absence: AI martial-arts apps exist, and reviews say their camera feedback feels wrong
repair.restated: AI martial-arts apps exist; the unmet need is feedback people trust
repair.proof: Review mining of the existing apps (the trust theme counted, as in the Phase 1 synthesis)

claims.claim: A phone camera scores a user's technique against elite practitioners in real time
claims.check: A review of five AI boxing apps found identical feedback across different videos and about 10 of 70 punches tracked; a single camera cannot see weight transfer (reviewer sells a rival app). A review of Zing found its camera claims misleading
claims.implication: Camera scores that feel wrong widen the trust gap that is PolySync's differentiator. Test slow techniques (stances, forms, guard) before fast strikes.

repair.fix: Score slow skills only (stances, guard, forms), with the club coach as the judge and the camera as an aid. Fast strikes wait for a second camera or a wearable motion sensor
repair.restated: A club coach scores slow techniques from phone video, assisted by pose overlays
repair.proof: Option A concierge test: 30%+ of 20 athletes would pay, and two coaches agree on the same clip

claims.claim: AI does 80% of coaching; a worldwide marketplace ranks coaches by credentials and outcomes
claims.check: Market size and commission figures were not verified. Only 10% of fitness participants prefer an AI-created workout to a human-led one. Two-sided marketplaces face cold start and off-platform leakage; ranking by outcomes rewards picking easy clients
claims.implication: It conflicts with ADR-009: the club is PolySync's coach supply. A global marketplace is a different company; sequence it after the console has active coaches.

repair.fix: Seed supply from coaches already on the console; charge a SaaS fee plus a booking fee to limit leakage; rank by outcomes adjusted for each athlete's starting level, not raw results
repair.restated: Console coaches can take athletes outside their club, ranked by credentials and risk-adjusted outcomes
repair.proof: 20+ active console coaches; athlete-coach pairs stay on-platform

claims.claim: Six scientific tiers (with population shares), assigned and updated automatically from performance data
claims.check: The framework is real. The population table is invented and contradicts itself (Tier 5 is 'top 0.0006%' and '~0.5%'). Tiers are defined by training volume and competition level, which a camera cannot observe
claims.implication: Use it as a self-reported onboarding question. Drop the population table and camera-assigned tiers.

repair.fix: Ask the tier at onboarding; update it from logged training volume and competition level, which the app already records. Delete the invented population table
repair.restated: Athletes self-report a McKay tier; the app suggests changes from logged volume and competition level
repair.proof: Self-reported tier matches the coach's assessment for most pilot athletes

claims.claim: Maldini averaged 0.56 challenges per game over his career; a Maldini-derived model tells a child '1.2 m too far from your mark'
claims.check: Event-level tackle data covers at most the end of a 1985-2009 career, so a career average cannot have been measured. The 'Golden Index' is a team-statistics z-score, not a golden ratio. A single phone camera cannot measure distance to a mark in play. Camera-based youth football apps already exist
claims.implication: Separate buyer (parents and academies), separate data, separate law: children's privacy and a named player's image rights. Not part of PolySync's launch.

repair.fix: Drop the named player and the statistic. Academy coaches teach defensive positioning principles, with licensed event data and consent owned by the academy
repair.restated: An academy product that helps coaches teach positioning, with consent, licensed data and no named-player likeness
repair.proof: Option B: one academy co-designs and pays

claims.claim: Users, including children, upload body photos for AI body-fat estimates and muscle grades
claims.check: Body-fat numbers from photos are unmeasured numbers, and body-composition feedback is an eating-disorder risk. Children's photos add children's-privacy law
claims.implication: Conflicts with two product principles already shipped: never show an unmeasured number; eating-disorder topics are hard-blocked. Adults only, photos on device, no body-fat numbers, if ever.

repair.fix: Adults only; photos never leave the device and are shown only as a private side-by-side, with no numbers; progress numbers come from measured inputs (tape, smart scale). Never children
repair.restated: Adults can keep private, on-device progress photos without any estimated numbers
repair.proof: Clinician sign-off on the flow; no rise in eating-disorder safety flags in a limited release

claims.narrative: Vision model trained on social video
claims.claim: Collect YouTube, Instagram and TikTok videos to train pose and technique models
claims.check: YouTube's terms prohibit scraping; third-party AI training is off by default unless each creator opts in. Academic datasets do not grant commercial rights
claims.implication: License datasets or capture consented footage with partner clubs.

repair.fix: Licensed datasets, footage captured with consent at partner clubs, and a creator programme with paid, opt-in licences
repair.restated: Technique models are trained only on licensed or consented footage
repair.proof: A signed data licence and a consent log that survives an audit

claims.claim: Launch across the Gulf, USA, EU, LatAm and Asia with local compliance; UAE health data must stay in the UAE
claims.check: The UAE law is real: Article 13 keeps health data in-country unless the health authority approves. Whether it reaches a wellness app is unsettled. Five regimes at once contradicts ADR-005 and ADR-006
claims.implication: Blind spot in our own plan: add Federal Law 2/2019 to the pilot's counsel questions (risk REG-03); plan UAE-region hosting or on-device processing.

repair.fix: One region per gate: UAE first with in-country hosting or on-device processing, then KSA, then the EU, then the US
repair.restated: PolySync launches in the UAE with health data kept in-country, and adds regions one at a time
repair.proof: Counsel's opinion on Federal Law 2/2019 for a wellness app; UAE-region hosting in place before the pilot

claims.claim: $19.99/month consumer price with event-triggered voice coaching at about $6 per user per month
claims.check: On the narrative's own numbers, voice alone is about 30% of the price, before app-store fees (15-30%), model calls and cloud GPUs for 3D replays
claims.implication: At the 2.9% download-to-paid median (ADR-010), acquisition cost must be near zero. Voice stays a later feature.

repair.fix: Voice becomes pre-recorded cues or on-device speech; revenue leads with the club tier, where acquisition cost is near zero
repair.restated: Club-led pricing with low-cost voice keeps gross margin healthy
repair.proof: Gross margin at pilot volume against a 70% target (our target, a hypothesis)

validated.finding: Strength and endurance interfere where it matters for athletes: power, and hard sessions close together
The engine blocks every unsafe plan in the eval set (7,877 of 7,877) and routes it to a coach
People want humans in their training: only 10% prefer an AI-created workout
Demand for hybrid racing is real and growing, including in the UAE
Consumer hybrid schedulers already exist at $9-10 a month, so the scheduler is not the moat

options.track: PolySync: hybrid engine + coach console, UAE pilot
options.test: The pilot as designed: 3 HYROX clubs, 8 weeks
options.kill: The pilot pass bars (checked in CI)

options.track: Technique drills for slow skills (stances, forms, guard), delivered through club coaches
options.test: Two-week concierge test: 20 athletes film shadowing; a human coach scores it; then ask them to pay
options.kill: Fewer than 30% would pay, or two coaches disagree on the same clip

options.track: Youth football through academies (the academy handles consent, not the app)
options.test: Two academy interviews and a letter of intent
options.kill: No academy will co-design or pay

options.test: Only after 20+ coaches actively use the console
options.kill: Coaches will not list, or athlete-coach pairs leave the platform

options.track: Social-video scraping, body-fat from photos, a named player's likeness, five regions at once

vision.what: The coach console and athlete app on the hybrid engine, in UAE HYROX clubs, with health data kept in-country and club-led pricing
Technique drills for slow skills, scored by the club's coach with the camera as an aid; self-reported athlete tiers; a consented, licensed footage dataset
vision.gate: Option A: 30%+ willing to pay; coaches agree on scores

vision.what: An academy product for youth football, with consent, licensed data and no named-player likeness
vision.gate: Option B: one academy co-designs and pays

vision.what: Console coaches can list beyond their club, ranked by credentials and risk-adjusted outcomes; KSA, then the EU
vision.gate: Option C: 20+ active console coaches; pairs stay on-platform

vision.what: Adults-only, on-device progress photos with no estimated numbers
vision.gate: Clinician sign-off; no rise in eating-disorder flags

corrections: The product name is PolySync, not 'Polysynce'.
HIPAA applies to covered entities and their business associates, not to health data in general; PolySync treats it as not applicable (operating decision, counsel to confirm).
Race claims such as 'first' or 'only' need a source; several competitors exist in every vertical the narrative names.
repairRule: Every claim has a repair path. Restating a claim does not validate it: a repaired claim counts as validated only when its evidence exists or its proof is observed. Tests decide; if a repair's proof fails, that line of the vision stops.

repairTypes.narrow: Keep the idea, shrink it to what works
repairTypes.new-method: Keep the goal, change how it is done
repairTypes.resequence: Keep it, do it later or one step at a time

pushback: Motivated reasoning: repairing claims to fit a vision decided in advance. The repair proofs are set before any data, and a failed proof stops that stage.
Capacity, not claims, is the binding limit: the repaired vision is still five businesses for one engineer. Stages run in sequence unless funding adds a team.
Body progress comes last on purpose: highest harm, lowest differentiation.
